_how_to_update: The self-hosting cost comparison on /self-hosting/. Same rules as pricing-comparison.json:
edit a figure, set its row's last_verified to the date you checked its source, set status,
and redeploy the assets. The page re-reads this file on load, so no Rust rebuild is needed.
Figures older than stale_after_days render with a visible recheck cue.
Every figure is a MONTHLY cost for a 1,000-device fleet, so the three options are comparable.
The server line uses the CHEAPEST tier of its published range on purpose. It is the number
least flattering to us, and a comparison that picks the flattering end is not worth writing.
Hours are deliberately NOT a figure here: they are the reader's, not ours. The page states
the loaded hourly band and lets them do their own arithmetic.
Where the figures come from. Ours is the Scale tier as src/views/pricing.rs prints it, which
is also the pidgeiot row's monthly total in pricing-comparison.json; all three must agree.
ThingsBoard's are the self-managed licence tab of thingsboard.io/pricing/, each row's source.
The analysis behind the page is outside this repo, in the pidgeiot-business directory beside
instead of paying', for the three options and the $20 to $40 server band, and section 1.3
(ThingsBoard, the primary competitor) for the $499 self-managed licence at 1,000 devices.
The $75 to $125 loaded hourly band is ../pidgeiot-business/payments-decision-2026-08.md
section 3a.5, 'Revised cost, with the engineering priced in'.
heading: What a thousand devices cost a month, before your time
subhead: Software licence, the server it runs on, and what that comes to before anyone is paid to look after it.

rows.note: Free software, and it ships custom dashboards we do not. Everything below this line is yours: upgrades, backups, TLS renewal, and the pager.
You pay for the licence and still run the machine, so the ops burden is identical to Community Edition.
33% under self-managed Professional Edition before a single hour is counted, and the hours below are ours rather than yours.

hours.heading: Then your hours, which nobody budgets
hours.body: Patching, upgrades, backups you have tested restoring, TLS renewal, and being the person who gets paged when ingestion stops. At $75 to $125 an hour, the loaded rate we use for our own build-versus-buy decisions, Community Edition costs what we charge at somewhere between two and a half and four and a half hours a month.

concession: If your own dashboards or owning the box matter more than those hours, self-host. We would rather you did that than pay us and resent it. Simplicity alone wins us nothing against software that is free and good.

exit.heading: The question worth asking instead
exit.body: Self-hosting is usually bought as insurance against being trapped. Ask about leaving instead: the wire protocol and API are documented and open, telemetry forwards to any InfluxDB-compatible store you own, and every device's history is exportable through the documented API. You can leave, which is worth more than being able to self-host.
